title: Quantification of interindividual variability in neuromuscular blockade following rocuronium administration: A prospective electromyographic analysis in patients undergoing general anaesthesia
summary:
Rocuronium is a medicine used during general anaesthesia to relax the muscles. It is required, among other purposes, to allow safe insertion of a breathing tube into the trachea. However, the strength and duration of muscle relaxation vary considerably between individual patients. Some of these differences may be caused by small inherited differences in the genetic material.

The study will include 400 patients scheduled for robot assisted removal of the prostate because of prostate cancer. All patients will receive rocuronium as part of their general anaesthesia. The usual total dose will be administered as two consecutive partial doses. This allows particularly accurate measurement of how strongly and how quickly the medicine acts in each patient.

Muscle responses will be measured using electrodes placed on the skin. In addition, a painless swab will be taken from the inside of the cheek before surgery. Only predefined regions of the genetic material that may influence the effects of rocuronium will be analysed. The entire genetic material will not be examined.

After surgery, recovery, pain, nausea, vomiting, confusion and postoperative complications will be assessed. A final telephone interview will be conducted 30 days after surgery. The aim is to better understand the reasons for differences in drug response and to support the future development of more individualised and safer dosing of muscle relaxants.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Male patients aged 35 to 80 years. Elective robot assisted radical prostatectomy for prostate cancer. Planned surgery under general anaesthesia. ASA physical status I to III. Written informed consent after oral and written information. Ability to understand the study information and to complete the questionnaires provided in German.
Exclusion criteria:
Missing or withdrawn written informed consent. Relevant language barrier preventing comprehension of the study information or completion of the questionnaires provided in German. Renal impairment greater than KDIGO stage 2. Neurological or neuromuscular disease. Diagnosed dementia or preoperative delirium. Body weight outside a range of plus or minus 20 percent of ideal body weight. Severe visual or hearing impairment preventing valid completion of study assessments. Known allergy or hypersensitivity to rocuronium or propofol. Concurrent participation in another interventional or experimental research study. ASA physical status greater than III.
